title: Mounties identify man killed by police and linked to Medicine Hat homicide
article: Mounties have confirmed the identity of the man shot and killed by a Medicine Hat cop, who may also be linked to a murder investigation.
Christopher Arkell, 50, was the man shot by police following a standoff on a rural property outside of the city, about 300 km southeast of Calgary, where Chester Hunchak's body was found.
RCMP Staff Sgt. Ron Campbell said an autopsy completed Wednesday in Calgary confirmed the death of 67-year-old Hunchak was a homicide.
However, authorities aren't disclosing the manner of his death at this time, he said.
"It's key evidence as far as the investigation goes and we don't want to impact the integrity of the investigation by releasing that information right now."
Last Saturday, RCMP were called to a residence just outside Medicine Hat city limits to support the Medicine Hat Police Service, who were conducting a missing person investigation.
During the investigation, Medicine Hat cops were confronted by an armed male, who has now been identified as Arkell.
Arkell threatened to shoot cops, according to Alberta Serious Incident Response Team (ASIRT), which is now investigating.
During the course of events, police saw Arkell pull a person that appeared to be unconscious or deceased from behind the residence and into their view.
Mounties said that person was Hunchak, who was already deceased.
Shortly after a further confrontation, Arkell was shot by a veteran male officer of the Medicine Hat force.
Because ASIRT is investigating the officer's actions, Campbell said no further details will be released by Mounties about the case.
Jeanine Hunchak, Chester Hunchak's daughter, said the person linked to her dad's death is not known to the family.
"I don't know him, I don't have a clue. I have no idea," she said.
"Whoever this dude is that killed my dad obviously had to shoot him with a gun, because there's no way that you'd kick my dad down."
Jeanine said she wants to know what happened but it's unimaginable her dad being overcome by someone without a weapon.
"My dad was a strong man. You don't mess him."
Authorities continue to investigate the homicide and the police-involved shooting.
